newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma to keep roads to Suu Kyi's home closed.
newsitem.headline: Burma to keep roads to Suu Kyi's home closed.

text.p: The Burmese government said on Saturday that roads leading to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's home will remain closed for security reasons.

"The barricades are there for security reasons and the personal security of the lady," a government spokesman told reporters at a monthly news conference. "When the situation improves, we will remove the barricades."
Access to Suu Kyi's lakeside home has been blocked since anti-government student unrest on the streets of Rangoon in early December.
The Nobel peace laureate has said that she is unhappy with the restrictions. Suu Kyi was unavailable to comment on the latest government statement.
The government spokesman also said that Burmese universities and colleges closed after the December protests would remain closed until "an appropriate time."
He also said the government had revealed a plot by a Thailand-based exiled students' movement to create disturbances in Burma and identified an American woman in Thailand as being involved.
